items.title: Sparsity is unchanged when all edges live on fewer than n vertex classes
items.author: Signe Lundqvist; Tovohery Randrianarisoa; Klara Stokes; Joannes Vermant
items.work: Sparsity greedoids and pebble game algorithms for posets
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 289-293: for parameters K and L satisfying the three numbered inequalities, if the edges of a graph are supported on the first t of the n vertex classes with t smaller than n, then the graph is sparse for K and L exactly when the graph on those t classes is sparse for the restricted parameters. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 294-308) is a subset-by-subset verification: after the immediate direction it reduces the claim to adding isolated vertices in a new class, and then bounds an arbitrary subset of the enlarged vertex set in three configurations, namely subsets contained in the old classes, subsets meeting two later classes, and subsets meeting the last old class together with a later one; the first numbered inequality is what absorbs the contribution of the later classes in the second and third configurations. The statement records only the equivalence.

primary.label: unlabelled lemma at source lines 289-293 (sparsity of a graph supported on a proper initial set of vertex classes)

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the unlabelled lemma, retained line for line

contexts.label: the numbered system of inequalities on the parameters, carrying the labels conditionposet1, conditionposet2 and conditionposet3-increasing, retained as context: the statement assumes it and the proof applies it at source lines 300 and 307
